features: Three curved raised primary arms meeting centrally
Counterclockwise outward sweep in chosen positive-relief top view
Three shallow inter-arm apical pits and subtle bullae
Fine ornament subordinate; no living tentacles
tribrachidium.claim: Original genus-level Tribrachidium fossil-form study, not a scan, exact specimen replica or settled living reconstruction. Affinity and feeding remain interpretations.
tribrachidium.observation: Personally inspected actual fossil panels A/B of2015 Fig1, separately from digital latex-cast-derived CFD panels C/D. A shows low circular relief with curved threefold branches and faint peripheral ornament; B has contrasting preservation. Text distinguishes primary arms, bullae and three shallow apical pits, with low ~2mm relief. Article states counterclockwise branch curvature, but fossil negative/positive orientation can invert apparent handedness. Chosen delivered geometry is explicitly a positive-relief original interpretation, not a claim that displayed negative fossils have same apparent chirality.
tribrachidium.decisions: Reject first generated concept pit-centered knobs, tree-like veins and overly thick relief. Second concept is useful for three low curved ridges, but still exaggerates pits and repeated ridge grooves; reduce both to shallow subordinate surface relief, no central knobs in pits. Single integrated surface avoids floating anatomical tubes. Palette artistic, 40mm nominal diameter.

features: Unequal serrated teeth and low cols
Two steep concave glacial hollows on opposite flanks
Noncompact elongated silhouette distinct from horn
arete-ridge.claim: Generic original deglaciated arête landform, not Garden Wall replica or exact locality, period or quantitative erosion model.
arete-ridge.observation: Personally read NPS distinction of long thin jagged crest between adjacent glaciers versus horn with at least3 glacial faces. Personally inspected actual Garden Wall NPS/Jacob W Frank photograph: extended jagged crest, low col, steep fluted headwalls and hollow below, not a single pyramidal peak.
arete-ridge.decisions: Use original elongated terrain volume with continuous jagged crest and concave hollows on both sides. Concept near-side repeated bowls are design guidance only; avoid periodic scallops and ensure no compact horn silhouette. Palette only, no copied snow/photo textures. Nominal landscape scale.

features: Visible breached levee and connecting channel
Unequal connected branches spreading onto floodplain
Low broad sandy depositional fan and tapering margins
crevasse-splay.claim: Generic original crevasse-splay process/form educational terrain. Natural levee interpretation is generic, not a precise Kinu artificial-levee site, disaster reconstruction, ancient cross-section or hydrodynamic simulation.
crevasse-splay.observation: USGS2024/1051 and other USGS pixel fetches failed403, not inspected. Personally read primary Izumida etal2017 and personally inspected Fig3 actual before/after orthophotos top row separately from DSM bottom. September2015 shows gap through artificial levee on river bank, scour reaching rightward, spreading pale sand lobes with unequal dark channels. Paper emphasizes artificial controls/buildings and erosion, so those exact site proportions and any natural-analogue equivalence are not assumed. USGS indexed primary text separately supports main channel, breach conduit and fan/bar linkage, not pixel evidence.
crevasse-splay.decisions: Original small natural-levee generic composition, based on published process linkage rather than replication of Kinu artificial embankment. Omit roads/buildings/canals/disaster debris. Concept reads branch fan but overstates levee height and simultaneous blue flow; reduce relief, use stylized shallow water as educational state without flow claims. Single clipped terrain/water geometry avoids coplanar layered strips.

features: Projecting resistant host beds above and below
Shorter near-orthogonal butt cleats terminate against face cleats
Irregular spaced cleated blocks, not decorative grid
coal-seam-outcrop.claim: Generic original human-scale coal seam outcrop form, not a named mine, age, coal rank, gas/permeability measurement or copied existing stratified cliff.
coal-seam-outcrop.observation: USGS fig25/AAPG and USGS PDFs return403 so not pixel-inspected. Personally inspected actual DOE/GSA report Fig18 p39, vertical outcrop photograph with dark coal face cleat below host rock and bedding-plane photograph with long FC and shorter staggered BC. Read text p37 describing systematic face versus shorter irregular terminating cross/butt cleats. Figure modified from Pashin etal2008; consult-only credit retained.
coal-seam-outcrop.decisions: Coal recess is real depth behind two host volumes. Unequal x/depth cleat block outlines, staggered terminating cross cuts, irregular chipped fronts; do not turn bedding-plane butt cleats into uniform horizontal brick courses. Concept has too many masonry-like horizontal coal splits; remove regular horizontal grid in geometry. No copied source pixels or regular decorative blocks.
